source: CDC Recommended Adult Immunization Schedule, ages 19+ (summarized for demo purposes)

rules.notes: Annual dose for all adults, ideally before end of October.
One dose of Tdap if never received, then Td or Tdap booster every 10 years.
2-dose series, doses 2-6 months apart, for all adults 50+.
Recommended at 65+ for everyone, or 19-64 with a qualifying chronic condition (e.g. diabetes).
Universal recommendation for adults 19-59 without prior vaccination/immunity (ACIP 2022 update). 60+ is risk-based shared decision-making.
Shared clinical decision-making for most adults; strongest benefit for 65+ or immunocompromised.
Adults born in/after 1957 need documented evidence of 2 doses or immunity; missing records are common and should be verified with the patient/provider, not assumed absent.
Adults without evidence of immunity or disease history need 2 doses; missing records are common and should be verified, not assumed absent.

Catch-up recommendation through age 26 (ages 27-45 are shared clinical decision-making, not modeled here - see known limitations). Simplification: ACIP actually requires 3 doses when the first dose was given at age 15+ and only 2 when started earlier; this rule always expects 2, which can under-flag a patient who should have a 3rd dose.

riskConditionKeywords: laboratory personnel routinely exposed to neisseria meningitidis
rules.notes: Not a general adult recommendation past the routine adolescent primary+booster (~11-12 and ~16) - minAge is set unreachably high on purpose so this only ever triggers through the risk-condition path. Risk groups: asplenia/complement deficiency/HIV, microbiologists routinely exposed to isolates, first-year college students in residence halls, military recruits, travelers to the meningitis belt. Simplification: real guidance calls for revaccination every 5 years while risk persists, which a single seriesDosesTotal:1 check doesn't capture.

riskConditionKeywords: laboratory personnel routinely exposed to neisseria meningitidis
rules.notes: Shared clinical decision-making for ages 16-23 (preferred 16-18) with no ongoing risk factor, or risk-based at any age for asplenia/complement deficiency or routine occupational exposure to isolates (lab personnel specifically - general clinical/healthcare work is NOT itself a standard indication, a common misconception). intervalMonths is set high because this isn't an annual/periodic vaccine like flu - a single documented dose (or shared-decision conversation) doesn't need to repeat.
